'''Bernhard Josef Philberth''' (26 March 1927 in [[Traunstein]], Germany – 8 August 2010<ref>{{cite web|url=http://tributes.heraldsun.com.au/obituaries/heraldsun-au/obituary.aspx?n%3Dbernhard-josef-philberth%26pid%3D144589026 |title=Father Bernhard Josef Philberth Obituary: View Bernhard Philberth's Obituary by Herald Sun |accessdate=2010-09-02 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110706104630/http://tributes.heraldsun.com.au/obituaries/heraldsun-au/obituary.aspx?n=bernhard-josef-philberth&pid=144589026 |archivedate=6 July 2011 |df=dmy }}</ref> in [[Melbourne]]) was an independent [[physicist]], engineer and philosopher. He was ordained a Roman Catholic priest in 1972.

==Biography==
Philberth was a member of the Academy of Science of Chieti (Italy), the Academy of Sciences of Besançon(France; where he was the first German to be accepted in a century), [[the Physical Society of Japan]] in Tokyo and the [[International Glaciological Society]] in London.

He was the originator of a project in the 1960s to investigate the disposal of [[radioactive waste]] deep inside stable, inland [[ice sheet]]s<ref>"Atomkernenergie" H.11/1956, H.3/1959</ref><ref>Académie des Sciences, Paris, C. R. 14/1959</ref> (presented by the French High Commissioner for Nuclear Energy).<ref>IAEO, Monaco Conference 1959</ref><ref>ETH-Referat Zurich 1960</ref> His brother, Prof Karl Philberth headed the thermal drilling program of the International Glaciological Greenland Expedition (EGIG) as part of the project.<ref>{{Cite magazine|title = These Priests' Invention Could Help Us Drill Into Icy Alien Worlds Someday|url = https://www.wired.com/2015/01/philberth-priests-probe-icy-moons-nuclear-waste/|magazine = WIRED|accessdate = 2015-10-21|date = 22 January 2015}}</ref>

In [[relativity physics]], Philberth discovered the "time gradient" ("Zeitgradient" in German)<ref>Académie des Sciences, Paris, C. R. 4/1963</ref> (presented by [[Louis de Broglie]]),<ref>Royal Academy of Science, Brussels, Bulletin 1964–5</ref> and the relationship between the electromagnetic fundamental values.<ref>Academy of Science, Genoa, Atti 1966</ref>
 
With his brother, he was granted over a hundred [[patent]]s for inventions in various areas of physics, such as the "[[cryobot]]" (also known as a Philberth probe) and the Philberth transformer.  He authored numerous technical publications on nuclear energy, energy management and patent law.

Philberth was also an environmentalist and initiated efforts to protect the environment using taxation law.<ref>"Städtehygiene", August 1967/H.8</ref> He made a submission to the [[Bundestag|Deutsche Bundestag]] which resulted in a change in oil tax and was the originator of taxation of lead in petrol<ref>"Städtehygiene", April 1972/H.4</ref> (law passed by the Bundestag in 1984).

As firm believers in philanthropy, the Philberth brothers founded of the "PH-Foundation" in the [[Philippines]], which sponsors the education of youths from disadvantaged families (with over 2,000 graduates to date).

He died on 8 August 2010 due to pneumonia.

* "Offenbarung"  ({{ISBN|0-646-20838-1}})  (EN: "Revelation" ({{ISBN|0-646-20837-3}}))
* "Der Souverän"  ({{ISBN|0-646-33833-1}}) (EN: "The Sovereign"  ({{ISBN|0-646-33834-X}}))
